Text-based games offer a rigorous testbed for language comprehension, reasoning, and autonomous planning. However, existing benchmarks rely on slow Python interpreters, restricting simulation speeds to approximately 0.1 steps per second. This limitation makes large-scale agent training impractical, as it necessitates consuming vast amounts of memory and computational energy. To address this, we introduce TextWorldExpress, a C++-based high-performance engine that executes game states up to 100,000 times faster than its Python counterpart, achieving a total acceleration ratio of 10,000x. This enhancement enables processing roughly 3 million text game interactions per second, facilitating the extensive training of artificial agents. Furthermore, we refine the TextWorld framework by adding 20 new tasks and complex subgoals to create more challenging environments. Our experiments demonstrate that TextWorldExpress supports the training of agents capable of mastering every task we propose.

Topological insulators are defined by a bulk band structure that supports a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ index, which can be determined via the bulk-edge correspondence as the sum of edge states' parity at the boundary. This study extends that correspondence to systems containing defects, demonstrating how to recover the original $\mathbb{Z}_2$ index by calculating parity across a specific set of surfaces. This proposed collection is termed an A-spatial approach. We validate this framework by modeling a 2D Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain with flaws, where the method successfully retrieves the correct $\mathbb{Z}_2$ index for both trivial and non-trivial bulk phases.

This paper establishes the constant overshoot o undershoot for constants Dirichlet boundary value problem for $p$-harmonic functions inside a planar sector. We explicitly calculate the limit as $r \to \infty$ of the ratio between two positive subsupersolution of the form $f(r,\theta)=r^{2/p-1}g(\theta)$, where $g$ is a positive trigonometric polynomial. We show that this ratio converges to a unique positive constant, which we call the overshoot undershoot ratio. This constant provides sharp bounds on the asymptotic behavior of the solution to the given boundary value problem.

This paper introduces a new multivariate spatial model designed to simulate extreme oceanic environments by employing multivariate extreme value distributions to conditionally sample peaks of significant wave height and peak period across space. The model's parameters are derived from the spatial extremes of a dataset representing significant wave height and peak period extracted from the EN4 reanalysis. Simulation results demonstrate the model's capacity to generate extreme wave fields that align with observed reality, specifically by accurately reflecting the localized nature of these extremes and the distinct zonal gradients evident in the study area.

This work presents a new proof of the Finiteness Theorem by Buium, which asserts that for any fixed polynomial $f \in \mathbb{Z}[u,v]$ and a given field of numbers $K$, there exist only a finite number of non-trivial solutions to the functional equation $f(f_K(x), f_K(x+\lambda)) = 0$. Here, $f_K$ represents Buium's extension of the polynomial into variables within the field $K$.

Operational safety is a primary concern for robots functioning in unstructured environments, particularly when humans guide them. While existing methods for teaching robots through demonstration often fail to account for variations in human-robot physical dynamics, this paper introduces a novel approach to motion adaptation that considers both spatial and temporal discrepancies caused by such variations. We propose a pipeline combining manifold-aware Iterative Closest Point (ICP) with kernelized parallel transport. While manifold-aware ICP aligns the demonstration's robot kinematic chain with the robot's body segments for spatial alignment, parallel transport maps the demonstration's joint velocities onto the target robot for temporal alignment. We validate this method using data from a push-task demonstration executed by a human on two different robot types, showing that the adapted movements remain within safety boundaries.

This study examines the Standard Model Higgs boson pair production and subsequent decay into $b\bar{b}$ and $WW^*$ modes at the LHC, utilizing the matrix element technique. The analysis employs a simplified model featuring a narrow-width approximation for on-shell intermediate Higgs bosons, with signal extraction performed using the matrix variable $m_{b\bar{b}}$. The study further investigates how the selection of specific kinematic cuts influences the signal-to-background ratio.

We introduce a novel method for estimating the 3D pose of everyday objects from a single image by utilizing a data distribution where the ground-truth orientation is misaligned with the implied semantics in the image captions. This approach requires no additional data collection or model training to align these truths with the text descriptions. Instead, we employ a pre-trained large-scale vision-language model to generate multiple new captions for each training sample, effectively creating a "misalignment" between an object's actual 3D position and its textual description. We demonstrate that this setup enables the accurate prediction of 3D rotation by leveraging the inherent diversity of pre-existing language variability.

The rapid dissemination of misinformation on social media has fueled widespread vaccine hesitancy, a problem that poses significant challenges to public health systems globally. This study introduces a novel approach to identifying individuals' acceptance of or resistance to the COVID-19 vaccine by analyzing their engagement with misinformation in Twitter conversations. We assembled a unique dataset comprising 11,000 tweets from 2,000 users, annotated for stance on vaccination, and developed a specialized dialogue identification model. This system leverages contextual information from surrounding dialogue to accurately predict user positions. Our findings demonstrate that the proposed method surpasses traditional stance detection techniques, achieving an F1 score of 0.813.

The production of isolated attosecond pulses via High-Harmonic Generation (HHG) is highly sensitive to fluctuations in the driving laser's intensity, a limitation that has historically required stabilizing the intensity within approximately 1%. This study introduces a novel strategy for HHH pulse control by coherently manipulating three fundamental components of the resulting spectrum—specifically, the amplitude of the carrier envelope, spectral phase, and spectral shape—through the robust field shaping of the input. This method successfully generates stable isolated attosecond pulses even when the driving laser intensity fluctuates by up to 20%.

The Algol system, a classic eclipsing binary, has recently been observed by the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS). This observation revealed a third body, designated Alg3, with a 1.2-day orbital period. Our analysis indicates that Alg3 is a low-mass companion weighing approximately 0.015 solar masses, orbiting at a distance of 0.03 astronomical units. We propose that this object is a brown dwarf or a very low-mass star, likely formed via the tidal disruption of a minor body during the system's evolution. Consequently, Alg3 should not be mistaken for a potential new Algol component resulting from mass transfer.

We examine the time-dependent non-linear Schr\"odinger equation within the exterior of a fixed smooth, bounded convex obstacle in $\mathbb{R}^3$, subject to Dirichlet boundary conditions. The equation features a smooth, supercritical power-type non-linearity. By applying a variational approach, we demonstrate the existence of a specific solution that exhibits blow-up in finite time at the equation's nonlinear threshold.

Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) have proven effective for solving partial differential equations (PDEs) across diverse fields, though they face limitations regarding solution accuracy when applied to complex PDEs with intricate geometries using uniform grids. This paper introduces a new vertex generation strategy called Residual-based Adaptive Grid Node Generation (RANG). The method adaptively refines PINNN training by dynamically adding nodes in areas exhibiting high residual errors, effectively functioning as an adaptive h-refinement technique. By concentrating computational resources on error-prone zones, RANG enhances training efficiency and accuracy. The approach was validated against three PDEs representing advection-diffusion equations, Helmholtz equation, and Darcy flow. Results demonstrate that RANG outperforms standard uniform grid strategies in both accuracy and computational speed.

This research presents a physics-based, multi-domain simulation of an n-type ferroelectric field-effect transistor (FeFET) utilizing a fully coupled, self-consistent solver for Poisson's equation and electron continuity equations. The study incorporates a comprehensive set of n-type FeFET physical phenomena, including quantum confinement, density of states, band structure engineering, band bending, band gap renormalization, band-to-band tunneling, Auger recombination, trap-assisted recombination, trap states, drift-diffusion transport, ferroelectric hysteresis, depolarization fields, and domain wall effects. A key focus is the analysis of adverse capacitance arising from the n-type domain wall, which results from the combined influence of quantum confinement and density of states. The simulation accurately models the dynamic evolution of domain walls in response to an applied gate voltage, capturing the transition from n-type to intrinsic and then to p-type domains. The resulting adverse capacitance manifests as a reduction in the effective gate voltage across the channel, leading to a non-linear gate response and a decrease in transconductance. The derived adverse capacitance model aligns well with experimental observations, and the simulated I-V characteristics agree closely with measured data.

This research introduces a novel Weakness Identification and Management (WI&M) methodology grounded in Knowledge Graph (KG) technology. The primary objective is to construct an Freight Ecosystem Dependency-Weakness KG (FED-WKG) to facilitate the analysis of weakness propagation within the freight ecosystem. The study outlines the comprehensive workflow for FED-WKG development, including Weakness Information Extraction (WIE), Weakness Relationship Extraction (WRE), and Weakness Property Extraction (WPE). The methodology employs an integrated approach combining Named Entity Recognition (NER), Relation Extraction (RE), and Knowledge Base Completion (KBC). The analysis reveals that the freight ecosystem exhibits a high degree of interdependence, where the failure of a single entity can trigger cascading effects across multiple downstream entities.

This study examines the ergodic characteristics of a stochastic Ginzburg-Landau equation driven by a compound Poisson process featuring unbounded variations. By employing a variational approach alongside the criteria developed by Li and Zhang, the authors establish the ergodicity of the corresponding mean-field dynamics. Subsequently, the irreducibility of an associated stochastic system—featuring pure jump perturbations and lacking pure death terms—is proven via a four-step methodology. Finally, the unique Li-Yorke chaotic behavior in the corresponding deterministic counterpart is achieved.

This paper presents a complete structural characterization of the least degree $\delta(\Gamma_G)$ for the power graph of any finite nilpotent group $G$. Additionally, we provide precise conditions to determine exactly when $\delta(\Gamma_G)$ equals $1$, $2$, or any specific integer $n \in \{1,2,\dots\}$.

This article outlines the design and scientific objectives of the SHiP experiment, which is scheduled to commence operations at the LHC in 2028. The facility will utilize a 40-meter-long, 2-meter-wide beam pipe situated between the SPS proton and nuclear collision points, with the forward debris from these collisions directed toward extensive downstream detectors. The compact intercolllimator space allows SHiP to access a unique forward kinematic regime, enabling the discovery of rare processes and the search for exotic particles produced in high-energy collisions. The article outlines the instrument's configuration, scientific goals, and the advancements in design and engineering undertaken to prepare for its deployment.

Point clouds represent a prevalent 3D data format, yet existing Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) for point cloud analysis remain constrained by significant drawbacks. These issues include the inability to handle arbitrary point cloud sizes, the generation of distorted graphs, and the excessive memory consumption associated with constructing adjacency matrices. To address these challenges, we introduce an innovative method for generating graphs that is both size-agnostic and resolution-enhanced. Furthermore, we propose a novel architecture designed specifically for processing point clouds, evaluating its performance against current state-of-the-art solutions on various tasks.

The paper introduces SLIM, a novel semantic-hostless Trojan assault that targets the control flow of host applications. This technique relies on a host's existing instruction set and register values to generate compact, evasive Control Flow Graphs (CFGs) trojaned by the attacker. SLIM trojans are undetectable by current signature-based tools, including dynamic analysis, because they lack traditional signatures and do not remain static. Furthermore, the paper presents a methodology for identifying and reversing these threats through a combination of data-driven and control-flow analysis.

The Remote Observatory Spectrograph Instrument for Integral Field Element (ROSIE) was originally developed for the Mauna Kea Observatories' Magellan Baade Spectrograph (MBCS) and has been integrated with the Remote Observatory Spectrograph Instrument for Integral Field Element (RMSIF) to form the Magellan Spectrograph for Remote Integral Field Observation (MRS-RMS). This instrument combines the capabilities of the MBCS with a custom-built lenslet array, enabling the acquisition of high-resolution, high signal-to-noise integral field spectroscopy (IFS) across the 300–1000 nm range. Designed to support the Measuring Energy of Stars and their Evolution (MESE) project, ROSIE offers a cost-effective method for obtaining extensive IFS data. This paper details the instrument's design, operational procedures, and performance characteristics.

This study examines the existing literature on carbon-carbon fusion, a reaction pivotal to the stellar nucleosynthesis of elements heavier than carbon. We demonstrate that the experimental data are consistent with theoretical models predicting a sub-barrier enhancement factor of $10^4$ to $10^5$ and a fusion half-barrier parameter of $S_0 = 1.0 \pm 0.1$. Furthermore, we explore how the Trojan Horse technique can be utilized to directly measure the fusion cross-section, thereby enabling a more precise determination of the half-barrier parameter.

We present high-resolution spectroscopic observations for 12 planet-host stars, utilizing the ESPaDOnS and HARPS instruments to determine their abundances of 13 elements. Our analysis reveals that all 12 stars exhibit significant chemical variability, with median dispersion reaching 0.25 dex for iron and 0.20 dex for magnesium. This heterogeneity is comparable to findings in the Sun's neighborhood and contradicts the assumption of uniform stellar composition. Consequently, these variations introduce substantial uncertainties into models estimating the internal structures of terrestrial exoplanets, as current models often rely on the premise of a homogeneous stellar makeup. We demonstrate that the uncertainty in a planet's core mass fraction can be as high as 10%, stemming from the uncertainty in the initial composition. To address this, we propose a new methodology that calculates core mass fractions by accounting for stellar chemical diversity, thereby enabling more accurate constraints on exoplanet interiors.

Commercial Wireless Fidelity (Wi-Fi) localisation exploits Channel State Information (CSI) from existing infrastructure to ascertain user locations, leveraging the multipath effects detailed within subcarrier signals for fine-grained positioning. This study introduces a positioning framework that utilizes a dual-layer attention mechanism to enhance these subcarrier features. The proposed system comprises two key components: first, a CNN-based encoder extracts robust features from CSI data, employing hierarchical attention to weigh the significance of individual subcarriers; second, a hierarchical attention module refines these extracted features to further boost localization precision. Evaluated against the CHANELSI dataset, the model achieved a 90th percentile error of 0.38 meters, surpassing existing state-of-the-art methods by approximately 15%.

This study introduces a general framework for modal logics, utilizing topological structures to define semantics. We demonstrate that this approach can determine the semantics for virtually all standard normal modal logics, along with several non-normal variants, relying exclusively on a complete first-order condition. Furthermore, we provide an alternative method to verify the completeness of various soundness proofs with respect to all corresponding classes of topological structures, utilizing model expansion.

The concept of edge-tinting on a graph $G=(V,E)$ involves assigning colors to edges such that every vertex $v$ is incident to edges of at most $\Delta(v)$ distinct colors, where $\Delta(v)$ represents the degree of $v$. A graph is deemed robustly edge-tintable if it possesses a valid tinting using exactly $\Delta_{\max}$ total colors, with $\Delta_{\max}$ being the maximum degree found within $G$. In 2019, Kalkowski, Kierstead, and Pfender established that every cubic bipartite graph is robustly edge-tintable with 3 colors. This study presents the first known example of a cubic bipartite graph that fails this property.

This study determines exact threshold values for functions on Hamming graphs $H_n(q)$, where $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and $q \in \mathbb{N}_{\ge 2}$. A graph's $s$-th order threshold for a function $f$ is the smallest average squared deviation from its mean, given that the function takes at most $s$ distinct values. We derive spectral conditions that characterize functions achieving this minimum, expressed solely through their Hamming distance Fourier coefficients. These coefficients correspond to the Fourier transform of $f$ relative to the irreducible characters of the graph's adjacency algebra. Our findings extend and generalize prior work by Calvo et al. (2019), who addressed the first-order case ($s=1$), and we provide explicit formulas for the first-order thresholds specifically for $q=2$.

COPASI is a highly capable simulation environment for biochemical networks, yet its desktop interface presents usability barriers for both general users and developers. To address this limitation, we introduce ShinyCOPASI, an intuitive web-based frontend that streamlines model exploration and result analysis. This platform supports interactive engagement with COPASI models via RESTful APIs, allowing users to modify simulation parameters, execute runs, and visualize outputs through dynamic graphs and tables. We have deployed ShinyCOPASI to host COPASI models submitted to BioModels, a major repository for these networks. This deployment enables users to access and investigate these models without local installation, while also facilitating the seamless integration of existing models into new research workflows.

The rapid advancement of Machine Learning (ML) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) has yielded sophisticated models capable of addressing complex challenges across diverse domains. However, these models frequently struggle to generalize effectively in real-world settings, particularly when facing distributional shifts between training and testing environments. While the impact of such shifts is often measured using standard metrics like accuracy or error rates, these metrics fail to address the fundamental issue of ambiguity regarding the correct solution. This paper introduces a framework designed to quantify the impact of ambiguity on model performance within scientific ML and AI applications. We examine multiple quantification strategies, including those rooted in information theory, and conduct a comprehensive analysis comparing various approaches. Finally, we outline a proposed methodology for ambiguity measurement and discuss its potential application within the field of computational biology.

In this paper, we construct the von Neumann algebra generated by regular elements within a compact quantum group. We determine the precise conditions under which this algebra falls into the types $II_\infty$ or $I_\lambda$ ($1 \leqslant \lambda < \infty$). Furthermore, we examine the spectrum of the scaling automorphism acting on both the resulting von Neumann algebras and their underlying algebras.

This study introduces a novel iteration method for computing the ergodic distribution in large-scale Markov chains and Markov decision processes (MDPs) by integrating the GMRES algorithm with strategy iteration. Leveraging a structured approach to construct GMRES systems, the method addresses both time- and memory-constraints inherent in large-scale scenarios. The proposed algorithm demonstrates superior performance compared to traditional GMRES iterations, particularly when the system matrix exhibits a high condition number. Additionally, the work provides a theoretical analysis of convergence for GMRES-based strategy iteration and establishes sufficient conditions under which convergence is guaranteed in finite steps.

This study introduces a novel Bayesian inverse method designed to simultaneously estimate unknown parameters within a time-series simulation model and the subsequent time-series data. By employing a contour estimation technique, we can resolve the challenging non-convex posterior landscape typical of such Bayesian inference tasks. Our approach is validated through numerical experiments, including the analysis of the widely recognized Lorenz-96 system.

This paper investigates the role of region-based overparameterization in enhancing the resilience of neural network training against adversarial examples. We demonstrate that while this overparameterization aids resistance, it does not guarantee a solution; rather, it facilitates the avoidance of spurious local minima that are highly vulnerable to attacks. Furthermore, we establish that the benefit of regional diversity in queries is not universal and depends on the specific nature of the attack.

This study examines how jets fragment within the quark-gluon medium by analyzing medium-modified photon-tagged jet substructure in lead-lead collisions at a center-of-mass energy per nucleon pair of $\sqrt{s_\mathrm{NN}} =$ 5.02 TeV. The analysis utilizes the ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider, focusing on events containing an isolated-photon tag to constrain the transverse momentum of the initial hard scattering. Comparisons between data and predictions from perturbative QCD models, which do not incorporate medium effects, reveal a significant modification of jet substructure in the central region. Specifically, the distribution of groomed fractional energy, denoted as $z_g$, shows a marked shift toward lower values in the central rapidity zone compared to perturbative expectations. This observation indicates that the parent parton of the reconstructed jet experienced substantial energy loss prior to hadronization in the medium.

This article establishes several applications concerning the summation of infinite sequences defined by polynomial rational weights, a method that extends the work presented in [1]. We further derive new identities involving multiple zeta functions with colored arguments, applying these results to generate novel relations within the framework of multiple q-zeta functions.

This study presents the first direct imaging of the companion to the M-dwarf WISEA J153429.75-104303.3 (hereafter W1534-1043), utilizing the Gemini North 8m telescope equipped with the NIRI instrument. The system, previously identified as a binary by Rieke et al. (2018) with a separation of 0.2 arcseconds, was notably absent in the M-dwarf W1534-1043 in the M-band data from the M-dwarf survey. The newly discovered companion is located 0.4 arcseconds away from the primary, a position that places it outside the field of view of the aforementioned survey. The object exhibits a contrast ratio of 1.4 magnitudes fainter than the primary in the M-band and 2.0 magnitudes in the Ks-band. Assuming a 0.04 arcsecond radius for the primary star, the companion's orbit corresponds to a semi-major axis of 0.04 arcseconds, which translates to a physical distance of approximately 0.04 AU. The authors suggest that the system's initial binary configuration may have been disrupted by a close encounter with a third body, potentially explaining the current orbital characteristics.

This study examines the production of pions, kaons, (anti-)protons, and $\phi$ mesons in Xe-Xe collisions at a center-of-mass energy per nucleon pair of $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.44$ TeV, utilizing data from the ALICE experiment at the LHC. The analysis focuses on the transverse momentum ($p_{\rm T}$) dependence of the yield ratios between these species and pions, as well as their elliptic anisotropy ($v_2$) ratios. Additionally, the findings are compared with predictions from the HIJING and AMPT models.

Interpolating parton distribution function (PDF) data is a critical task for generating PDF sets, yet existing methods often fail to account for PDFs' specific characteristics. This study introduces an effective interpolation strategy that leverages the partial wave expansion to generate PDFs from discrete experimental data points. We demonstrate that this new approach outperforms standard techniques, such as cubic spline interpolation, in accuracy. Furthermore, we outline the requirements for constructing PDFs and present the updated EPPS19 PDF set, which incorporates recent experimental results.

This study examines how sintering temperature affects the microstructure and mechanical properties of compacted lunar and Martian regolith simulants. Utilizing thermal analysis, scanning electron microscopy, and mechanical testing, the research demonstrates that increasing sintering heat promotes the growth of larger particles and stronger interparticle bonds, which significantly enhances both compressive and flexural strength. Notably, for both types of simulant, optimal mechanical performance is achieved at 850 °C. Additionally, the microstructural evolution observed in the Martian simulant provides critical insights into the potential formation of sintered rock bridges on the Martian surface.

This study examines the instability of a liquid layer coating a cylindrical fiber, where the slip length at the solid-liquid interface is treated as a variable. The analysis reveals that the growth rate of the most unstable disturbance increases with higher slip values, thereby accelerating the onset of Rayleigh-Plateau instability. Furthermore, an analytical framework is developed to predict the wavelength of the dominant unstable mode, demonstrating strong agreement with numerical simulations.

This study utilizes the benchmark of the Brackett-$\gamma$ line to evaluate the star formation rates (SFR) derived from spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting for 100 galaxies within the COSMOS field. The sample, drawn from the COSMOS2015 catalog, comprises galaxies with redshifts $0.1 < z < 0.3$ and $10^{9} < \text{L}_{\text{Br}\gamma}/L_{\odot} < 10^{10.5}$, observed by the KMOS instrument as part of the COSMOS-Deep project. The Br$\gamma$ line serves as a robust tracer of SFR because it is less susceptible to dust extinction than other infrared recombination lines. We compare the Br$\gamma$-based SFRs with those obtained from SED fitting using the LePhare code, which incorporates UV, optical, and IR data from COSMOS2015. The analysis reveals a strong correlation between the two methods, with a scatter of 0.2 dex. The Br$\gamma$-derived SFRs are generally consistent with the LePhare results, though they tend to be slightly higher for galaxies with lower SFRs and lower for those with higher SFRs.

This article serves as the first installment in a two-part study dedicated to classifying unitary $\mathfrak{sl}_N$ subgroups within rational conformal field theories (RCFTs) characterized by a large level $k$. We concentrate specifically on type $II$ subgroups, which establish a one-to-one correspondence between the characters of the parent theory and regional modules of the subtype. These symmetries permit the construction of an extensive set of automorphisms acting on the regional module category; we analyze these explicitly for the case of $\mathfrak{sl}_N$. Furthermore, we demonstrate that such automorphisms are essentially limited to those already inherent to the theory. The conceptual framework developed here will be utilized in the following paper to achieve the overall classification.

This study introduces a novel methodology for solving the universal differential equation (UDE) framework across various classification and regression tasks. The proposed approach, termed the Universal Diffusion Algorithm (UDA), integrates a novel diffusion process into a UDE model. The core mechanism involves generating a latent representation for each input sample, which is subsequently projected back into the original feature space to produce output predictions. The UDA demonstrates superior performance compared to existing methods, including standard models and the URE-Karras approach, across a range of datasets.

This paper introduces a novel approach for recognizing handwritten mathematical expressions by processing image data captured from tablets and other writing tools. The study focuses on the specific challenge of identifying complex formulas, including fractions and integrals, within the mathematical domain. The authors propose a new system capable of detecting these intricate structures, leveraging sensor-derived information to generate the necessary visual inputs for expression recognition.

The study focuses on the specific challenge of identifying complex formulas, including fractions and integrals, within the mathematical domain. The authors propose a new system capable of detecting these intricate structures, leveraging sensor-derived information to generate the necessary visual inputs for expression recognition.

This paper introduces a novel, non-statistical technique for generating variable-duration synthetic speech from fixed-length inputs using the Mosaic Pitch-Spectrum Unit (PSU) framework. We challenge the prevailing assumption that duration manipulation relies on probabilistic models by demonstrating that a median-based strategy effectively achieves this goal. The proposed method integrates audio segments of equal duration through a two-stage process: initial duration adjustment via median calculation, followed by concatenation guided by a decision tree. Evaluated on the NIST SRE 2008/2004 datasets, the system demonstrates performance comparable to statistical alternatives, achieving equal error rates (EER) of 2.48% and 2.51% respectively.

This manuscript introduces the "spOccupancy" R package, which is designed to facilitate the analysis of species distribution data using occupancy models. We provide a detailed overview of the package's core functionalities and spatial modeling capabilities, illustrated through practical examples utilizing its built-in datasets. The "spOccupancy" suite supports various modeling strategies, including single-species and multi-species frameworks with spatial covariates, models accounting for spatially correlated detection errors, spatially explicit occupancy models, and integrated approaches that combine spatial occupancy with other data sources. Furthermore, we offer an online tutorial at http://www.marcobeyer.de/spOccupancy/ to assist users in effectively employing these tools.

Dermoscopy serves as a standard for diagnosing skin lesions, utilizing a dermoscope to enhance the visibility of subsurface structures that aid in identifying cancerous lesions. However, this method relies on specialized equipment and trained professionals, creating a barrier for individuals in areas lacking access to such resources. To address this, we introduce the Skincare initiative, an interactive deep learning framework designed to identify and classify skin lesions from dermoscopic images. This system integrates multiple deep learning models to detect lesions, differentiate malignancies, and locate specific features within the imagery. By incorporating a user interface, it empowers laypeople to obtain preliminary diagnostic insights, thereby reducing the need for immediate specialist consultation. This paper details the architecture and implementation of Skincare, with its source code available at https://github.com/CSAIL-MedAI/Skincare.

This study introduces a novel methodology utilizing a stochastic autoencoder to forecast the evolution of Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) from a solitary spectrum. We constructed a training set comprising 1,000 synthetic spectra generated via the spectral synthesis code SNFactory, which simulates SNe Ia explosions across the 1999–2020 timeframe. The resulting autoencoder network, featuring 100 hidden nodes, successfully reconstructs the full spectral profiles of these synthetic data. Furthermore, the model effectively predicts the time series for absorption features (such as Si II $\lambda$6355, Ca II H&K, and Fe II multiplets) and emission features (such as H$\alpha$ and [O I] $\lambda$6300) for every wavelength. We anticipate that this technique will facilitate the analysis of extensive SN Ia spectral datasets and aid in planning future observational campaigns.

We report the detection of a neutral carbon (C I) spectral line from a heavily obscured, gravitationally lensed star at redshift z = 2.09, which is attributed to the massive star IRC-15999G. This detection was achieved using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) at a resolution of 0.02 arcseconds, corresponding to approximately 40 AU. The observed profile exhibits a double-peaked structure with a full width at half maximum (FWHM) of 0.018 arcseconds and a peak flux ratio of 1.4. We attribute this morphology to the combined effects of the source's intrinsic variability and the magnification pattern of the lensing caustic network. The source's intrinsic variability is likely driven by pulsational mass loss or a binary companion system. Furthermore, the measured line width indicates that the outflow velocity from the star reaches 100 km/s, a speed sufficient to overcome the escape velocity from the star's immediate vicinity.

This study examines the vertical motion of inertial particles within turbulent, buoyant plumes using direct numerical simulations. The particles, which are neutrally buoyant and possess a finite size, are incorporated into the flow across a range of Stokes numbers ($\text{Re}_\tau$) and volume fractions ($\phi$). The results indicate that particle addition enhances the plume's entrainment and accelerates its rise velocity. Specifically, the growth rate of the plume width increases by a factor of $1 + 2.5\phi$, while the growth rate of velocity increases by $1 + 1.5\phi$. This enhancement stems from the particles' tendency to migrate toward high-strain regions, thereby intensifying the local turbulent kinetic energy and promoting mixing. The findings provide significant insights into particle-laden plume dynamics, with potential applications to volcanic eruptions and the release of aerosols from fires.

The spread of infectious diseases within a population is frequently modeled as a branching process, where the expected number of secondary infections, denoted by the basic reproduction number $R_0$, dictates whether an epidemic persists or fades. When $R_0$ exceeds one, the outbreak typically spreads indefinitely; conversely, if it falls below one, the infection eventually disappears. This paper investigates the extinction of infections within a homogeneous SIR framework operating on hypergraphs. We establish that if the spectral radius of the largest irreducible eigenvalue associated with the next-generation operator is less than unity, extinction occurs almost surely. Furthermore, we provide conditions under which this bound is both necessary and sufficient. Our findings extend and generalize prior research by Kudo and others, which were limited to standard graphs.

The recent discovery of a two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals ferromagnet, chromium triiodide (CrI3), has generated significant interest. This material is distinguished by its strong exchange interactions, which facilitate robust magnetism, and its Rashba effect, which arises from the lack of local inversion symmetry at the atomic sites. In this study, we examine the magnetization profile across the CrI3 lattice, specifically focusing on how the spin orientation of chromium atoms varies within the material's thickness. We demonstrate that the spin orientation of interlayer chromium atoms is dictated by the relative alignment of the outer layers, whether they are parallel (FM) or anti-parallel (AFM). Furthermore, we show that the FM state exhibits a net non-zero total magnetic moment, whereas the AFM state possesses a near-zero total moment. These findings offer valuable insights for the spintronic applications of 2D ferromagnets.

Differential rotation is a fundamental driver of magnetic activity in solar-type stars, yet the specific nature of this differential rotation in stars rotating more slowly than the Sun remains uncertain. This study examines the effects of anti-solar differential rotation—where equatorial regions rotate more slowly than polar regions—using direct numerical simulations within a global mean-field dynamo framework. We find that anti-solar shear does not prevent the emergence of global magnetic cycles; instead, it reverses the polarity of the magnetic field at the surface compared to the solar case. Additionally, magnetic activity concentrates at high latitudes rather than the equator, forming distinct bands that mirror solar facular zones but with opposite latitudinal preference. Although the anti-solar differential rotation suppresses the amplitude of the global magnetic field, it amplifies the radial dipole component, creating a magnetic configuration reminiscent of those observed in certain cool stars. Consequently, magnetic cycles driven by anti-solar differential rotation could potentially be mistaken for standard solar-type cycles in stellar observations.

Although deep learning has achieved remarkable success in various image and signal processing fields, the majority of existing methods focus exclusively on unimodal inputs and exclusively on unimodal outputs. Consequently, these approaches often fail to fully leverage complementary information from multiple data sources or fully address situations where various modalities are present at the output stage. To overcome these limitations, this paper introduces a novel Universal K-fan Multimodal Deep framework (UKF-DF). This architecture is designed to flexibly accommodate scenarios involving inputs and/or outputs across K different modalities. Specifically, the framework comprises two primary components: the K-fan structure, which facilitates the integration of diverse input modalities, and the shared representation learning mechanism, which enhances the extraction of discriminative features. The framework's versatility is demonstrated through three applications: single-input multimodal-outputs (SIMO), multimodal-input single-output (MISO), and multimodal-input multimodal-output (MIMO). Experimental validation using two distinct datasets confirms that the proposed method significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques.

Multithreaded programs introduce concurrency bugs that frequently cause elusive runtime failures, making them difficult to detect. While Dynamic Partial Order Reduction (DPOR) has emerged as a leading technique for verifying concurrent programs by eliminating equivalent execution traces, existing implementations suffer from low scalability due to the processing of irrelevant events. This paper introduces McMini, a DPOR engine built on top of the widely-used miniBDD library, which offers a configurable environment for future enhancements. McMini achieves a significant performance breakthrough by drastically reducing the count of equivalent executions processed during analysis. Implemented using region-based locking information to refine the program's interference model, it delivers a substantial speedup over current state-of-the-art tools, demonstrating top-tier results on both synthetic benchmarks and real-world case studies.

The rapid dissemination of unverified information on social media has prompted platforms like WhatsApp to implement technical restrictions on message forwarding. This study examines the efficacy of limiting the number of message forwards in curbing misinformation sharing. Our research indicates that such measures are largely ineffective because the reduced reach fails to alter user behavior; specifically, individuals who are prone to sharing false information remain active even after these restrictions are applied.

We examine a model of neutral genetic evolution within a general branching population framework, where individuals reproduce according to a given branching mechanism and their offspring receive types via a general branching mechanism with a Galton-Watson mean measure. Assuming the reproduction process is supercritical, we derive the asymptotic behavior of the Allelic Frequency Spectrum (AFS) as time progresses indefinitely. Specifically, we establish an equivalent asymptotic expression for the AFS in terms of the reproductive mean's characteristics near criticality and the branching mechanism. These findings generalize and extend previous work by Kyprianou and Papapantoleon, originally limited to Aveson branching processes with linear migration, to cover a broader class of populations.

Deep learning has become a dominant force in spoofing attacks, yet it simultaneously powers the most effective spoofing detection countermeasures. This duality stems from the fact that synthetic speech, audio, and face data harbor telltale artifacts of forgery. However, because these forged signals often closely resemble human traits, traditional models trained to identify them frequently falter in real-world scenarios. To address this limitation, we introduce a novel "Vigilant Activation Function" designed to refine the detection capabilities of deep neural networks. By dynamically adjusting the learnable parameters within a network's activation functions, this approach heightens sensitivity to subtle anomalies. We demonstrate its efficacy across end-to-end detection frameworks for both voice and facial forgery identification, showing significant performance gains.

We investigate locally supersymmetric models of inflation, specifically those driven by a Goldstino and a supergravity multiplet. By applying an efficient field transformation, we derive the scalar potential for a broad class of these theories. Our findings indicate that while many supersymmetric Goldstino-based inflation models fail to produce a positive scalar potential, locally supersymmetric constructions often succeed in doing so. We present several locally supersymmetric efficient field theories capable of realizing inflation, with specific examples providing excellent fits to observational data.

We introduce a novel quantum optical effect characterized by asymmetric second-order correlation functions between two single-photon sources. This effect is driven by a quantum interference mechanism that allows us to interpret the photon pair correlations as an interference pattern, where the asymmetry emerges from the distinct spatial locations of the individual sources. This phenomenon offers a fresh perspective on quantum optics and provides an accessible educational tool for illustrating nonclassical light properties and the spatial aspects of quantum interference.

This work introduces an original technique for characterizing planar microwave resonators, leveraging a scanning near-field terahertz probe to map the fields of high-Q superconducting resonators. By applying this method, we measured the inductance and dielectric loss tangent of the device, achieving a dielectric loss tangent precision of $10^{-6}$. These findings are compared against simulations and bulk material properties to validate the approach.

This paper presents a proof of the theorem by Erdős and Shelah, which establishes the existence of Borel functions $f$ and $g$ on the set of real numbers, $\mathbb{R}$, such that the induced family of Borel sets $\mathcal{B} = \{f^{-1}(A) : A \in \mathcal{A}\}$ satisfies the condition that for any distinct $A$ and $B$ in $\mathcal{B}$, the intersection of $A$ and $g^{-1}(A)$ with $B$ has a Lebesgue measure of zero. These findings were developed within the framework of work by Cichoń and Kojman.

This study examines whether introducing new trading tactics can generate superior performance by building upon the success of established methods. We employ a multi-agent simulation featuring 100 individual traders, each utilizing a distinct strategy to determine transactions. Initially, we establish a baseline using the "trend following" approach, which has been proven effective in prior research. Subsequently, we simulate the evolution of trader behavior over 100 years, allowing agents to develop their specific rules based on historical data. The results indicate that while the collective portfolio of all 100 agents outperforms a market consisting solely of trend followers, the primary driver of this success is the initial trend following group. In contrast, the remaining 99 agents, representing diverse and varied tactics, yield only marginal improvements.

Dynamic protocol identification represents a critical component of modern network security monitoring, yet it remains vulnerable to attacks that inject traffic to bypass identification mechanisms. This paper introduces a novel attack methodology designed to compromise the assault resistance of dynamic identification. The authors present results from experiments conducted on widely used open-source tools, demonstrating that current systems are susceptible to such exploits. The study concludes by offering recommendations to bolster the dynamic protection of network defense systems.

The effective control of magnons through proximitization with a superconductor is examined. This analysis demonstrates that a normal metal layer, situated between the superconductor and the magnetic material, is essential to suppress the detrimental effects of the exchange field. Furthermore, we investigate magnon gating using a normal metal gate and reveal that this mechanism relies on the exchange field suppression as well. These findings offer a pathway for utilizing superconductors in the development of hybrid magnonic-superconducting devices.

This study addresses a challenge in real-world machine learning: the introduction of new, unseen categories after an initial model has been trained. Although various strategies exist, most are constrained by a reliance on labeled data for both initial training and subsequent updates, necessitating data for these approaches. We introduce a zero-shot framework designed to handle novel class introduction without requiring additional training labels. Instead, this method leverages a pre-existing vocabulary of class descriptions to align learned representations with their corresponding labels. We evaluate this technique on the task of retraining classifiers for the AudioSet dataset after partitioning it into mutually exclusive sub-collections. Results indicate that zero-shot learning significantly outperforms standard retraining methods that depend entirely on data-driven label inference.

This work introduces a new metric for evaluating the entanglement of arbitrary $N$-qubit states within the Schmidt decomposition framework. We demonstrate that this measure is monogamously linked to the entanglement found in the optimal Schmidt partitions of the quantum state. Its validity is verified through applications to specific high-dimensional GHZ and GHZ-classified states. We anticipate this proposed tool will prove essential for analyzing entanglement in multi-qubit systems across various quantum computing and quantum information contexts.

This study introduces a cascaded-channel framework designed to model the propagation characteristics between an Intelligent Reflecting Surface (IRS) and a base station (BS), as well as between the IRS and mobile users. Utilizing this channel model, the paper proposes a low-complexity algorithm for jointly optimizing the transmit precoder at the BS and the configuration of IRS reflective elements to maximize the system's sum rate. Additionally, the proposed scheme is extended to a scenario involving imperfect channel state information.

This paper examines the relationship between regional U.S. online news coverage and COVID-19 outcomes, alongside the impact of the pandemic on news consumption patterns. Utilizing data from 1,000 domains across 250 U.S. regions, we analyzed over 1.5 million articles published between March 2020 and February 2021. Our findings indicate that areas with higher COVID-19 case and death rates experienced significantly increased news coverage of the virus, even after accounting for pre-existing levels of online news coverage. Conversely, the rise in the pandemic's cases and fatalities led to a decline in audience engagement with these regional news sources.

Counting represents a fundamental yet complex cognitive skill that develops gradually in early childhood. This study investigates such progression through a novel lens, employing a deep learning framework designed to master the base-10 system. Specifically, we utilize Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) enhanced with memory mechanisms to represent the internal states of a "counting agent." By examining the internal representations within these agents, we gain insights into the numerical cognition of artificial systems. Our findings indicate that agents can successfully master counting by integrating two key elements: an internal state encoding numerical magnitude and an external counter tracking the sequence. We further explore how varying architectural choices in the internal magnitude encoding correlate with specific developmental stages of counting observed in human children.

This paper introduces the "xor filter," a space-efficient and swift probabilistic data structure designed to determine if a given element is a member of an unspecified set. We demonstrate that this approach surpasses existing methods, including Bloom, Cuckoo, and standard Bloom Cuckoo filters, by offering superior speed and a reduced memory footprint. Theoretically, we establish the space and time complexity bounds, proving that space requirements scale as $O(n\epsilon\log(1/\epsilon))$ and query time scales as $O(c\log(1/\epsilon))$, where $n$ represents the number of filtered elements, $\epsilon$ denotes the false positive rate, and $c$ is the number of bits per filter word. We further provide a rigorous lower bound of $\Omega(n\epsilon\log(1/\epsilon))$ for the space complexity. Empirical evaluations confirm that the proposed method outperforms current state-of-the-art filters, achieving less than 1 byte of space per element while maintaining sub-millisecond query latencies.

This expository text examines the link between convex analysis and Hodge theory, focusing on how convex analysis applies to the study of algebraic geometry and holomorphic functions.

This paper introduces a novel methodology for analyzing market trends by examining the temporal progression of trades, modeled as a sequence consisting of trade direction (long or short), volume, and execution price. The proposed framework utilizes a sequence-to-sequence approach to forecast the trend data following a trade, where each element of this derived data represents a trade count within a specific post-trade time window. The research evaluates this methodology using historical data from the Canadian Exchange (CEMX), covering trades from 2012 to 2017. The findings demonstrate that the resulting trend data exhibits significant predictive power regarding future price movements. Furthermore, the study investigates the impact of this data on market efficiency and the potential for arbitrage opportunities.

Federated Learning (FL) has emerged as a robust machine learning paradigm that secures user privacy while enabling the training of models across distributed devices. However, FL faces significant challenges from malicious participants who may attempt to sabotage the learning process. To address this, numerous strategies have been introduced to detect and neutralize such threats. In this paper, we present FLVoogd, a novel system that integrates Byzantine fault tolerance with privacy preservation. FLVoogd combines Secure Multi-Party Computation (SMC) with aggregation techniques that maintain confidentiality while ensuring the final model remains robust against attacks. Our system successfully withstands various malicious behaviors, including data poisoning, model poisoning, and the inference of gradient-based user information. Additionally, FLVoogd innovatively mitigates the high communication costs inherent in SMC by employing differential privacy to selectively disable SMC for remote users exhibiting normal behavior. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that FLVoogd tolerates up to a quarter of malicious clients, achieves a 4.5-fold reduction in communication complexity, and maintains strong security guarantees.

This study introduces a novel, model-free, end-to-end autonomous navigation system designed for both real-world and simulated environments, specifically targeting a "pick-and-place" task. The system utilizes a camera to capture an image gradient pointing toward a target object, enabling the robot to move accordingly. The underlying concept involves transferring learned policies from a photorealistic simulation to the actual hardware through a shared gradient representation of the environment, effectively bridging the "sim2real" gap by relying on a single, unified learning signal. The proposed method employs a two-stage training process: initially, a navigation policy is developed in simulation using a photorealistic renderer, and subsequently, a translation layer is trained to align simulated states with real-world observations by matching gradient representations. Experimental results demonstrate that this approach successfully enables a robot to navigate and execute the pick-and-place task in reality, utilizing a policy originally trained solely in simulation.

Deepfake technology employs deep learning to generate or alter media files, such as images and videos, resulting in forgery. While numerous studies have addressed various aspects of this issue, the majority of existing detection models are tested on unconstrained data. This paper introduces the Media-Forger system, a unified framework for both creating and detecting deepfakes. It includes a comprehensive suite of tools designed to identify synthetic content across three domains: video-to-video editing, video generation, and audio synthesis. The system's detection component is highly robust, having been validated on challenging unconstrained datasets. Additionally, the authors have released the Media-Forger as open-source software to empower the community in advancing research on synthetic media detection.

Recent studies have established that the atmospheres of exoplanets are dynamically active, with circulation patterns heavily influenced by the balance between planetary rotation and atmospheric heating. This study investigates the physical states of exoplanetary atmospheres by examining the transit signatures of chemical equilibrium, specifically focusing on solubility equilibria versus gas-phase thermodynamics. We demonstrate that on temperate sub-Neptunes, the presence of a hydrogen-dominated atmosphere with a temperature of 300 K and a pressure of 1 bar can yield observable variations in the effective radius of the planet across different wavelengths. These variations arise from the formation of clouds in the upper atmosphere, driven by the solubility equilibrium of species such as water, ammonia, and hydrogen sulfide. Our findings indicate that the resulting spectral features are highly sensitive to the metallicity of the atmosphere and the specific abundances of these elements. Consequently, the detection of cloud-induced transit variations offers a powerful method for characterizing the atmospheric composition and physical properties of sub-Neptune-sized exoplanets.

This work presents a foundational study on the fundamental capabilities of simple, unsupervised, and unsupervised networks of excitatory and inhibitory neurons. We introduce a novel spiking plasticity framework that enables the generation of biologically plausible sequential patterns, such as those resembling motor behaviors, without relying on external supervision. The proposed learning rules emerge from a specific objective function that simultaneously promotes the formation of distinct internal representations and minimizes redundant information between them, aligning with known biological constraints for synaptic updates. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a two-dimensional world navigation task, where a robot explores an environment and learns to produce sequential spike-based movement commands.

This document details the "Out-of-Context" (OOC) challenge, an initiative designed to evaluate large language models (LLMs) in scenarios involving potential deception. Participants were tasked with three sub-tasks: (1) identifying passages from Wikipedia that could mislead a human, (2) crafting specific types of misleading sentences for LLMs, and (3) detecting such created passages. For each task, participants submitted both their model code and prompts used to generate outputs. The study assessed various prompting techniques, including zero-shot, few-shot, and methods employing external knowledge or self-consistency checks. The analysis revealed that zero-shot generation performed best for creating deceptive content, while incorporating external information significantly improved an explainer's ability to detect deception. The report concludes by offering recommendations for future research aimed at building more robust and explainer-friendly AI systems.

This study introduces an efficient approach for verifying solutions to parametrically dependent partial differential equations (PDEs) using spectral element methods combined with generalized polynomial chaos expansions (gPEs). The framework enables the detection of issues stemming from inadequate sampling of random inputs, poor polynomial approximations, insufficient spatial resolution, and violations of boundary conditions within a stochastic finite element context. The methodology is validated through two representative cases: a one-dimensional advection-diffusion problem and a two-dimensional Stokes system.

This paper introduces a sequential identification and isolation method for mean shifts in a multivariate Gaussian process, characterized by the fact that only a subset of components is directly observable. The proposed Adaptive Partially-Observed Sequential Probability Ratio Test (APO-SCRPT) accounts for the uncertainty inherent in unobserved dimensions, thereby enhancing detection performance. The effectiveness of this approach is validated through simulations and a practical application involving the monitoring of a multi-sensor system used for detecting leaks in a pipeline.

Dwarf galaxies serve as critical laboratories for investigating the chemical evolution of both individual systems and the broader universe. This study reviews current knowledge regarding dwarf galaxies, emphasizing their structural and chemical characteristics, while also addressing the observational and theoretical advancements necessary to deepen our understanding of their star formation and chemical enrichment processes.

We introduce a version of the homotopy action spectrum $\mathcal{F}_G$ for a profinite group $G$, designed to function as an "action spectral sequence" analog for homotopy fixed point spectra. We establish that the natural map from $E^{hG}$ to $\mathcal{F}_G(E)$ is a weak equivalence whenever $E$ possesses finite $p$-typical Lichtenbaum–Quillen type for some prime $p$, and we demonstrate the utility of this framework through various examples.

Extracting structured information from documents is a difficult yet vital task with numerous practical applications. While deep learning has shown great promise in this domain, it relies heavily on labor-intensive, costly, and time-consuming labeled data. This study introduces a cost-effective framework that enhances the labeling efficiency of visual-focused document extraction models. We achieve this by initially pre-training a model on a vast collection of unlabeled documents and then fine-tuning it with a minimal set of labeled documents. We evaluate our approach using the FIQA 2021 challenge, which involves extracting key-value pairs from invoices. Our results demonstrate that the method is both effective and versatile, capable of being applied to various visual-rich documents, such as receipts and medical bills.

Indium antimonide (InAs) serves as a promising substrate for growing rare-earth transition metal (RTM) oxides, which are renowned for their robust magnetism and significant spin-orbit coupling. To enable the development of advanced spintronic devices, it is essential to understand the bonding characteristics and electronic structures at RTM oxide/InAs interfaces. This study employs first-principles calculations to examine the interface between europium sulfide (EuS), a well-known ferromagnet, and InAs. We investigated two configurations: one where the EuS (111) surface bonds to the InAs (111) surface, and another where it bonds to the InAs (110) surface. Analysis of the electronic framework reveals that in the (111)/(111) arrangement, InAs retains its semiconducting properties, whereas in the (111)/(110) arrangement, InAs transforms into a metallic state. Additionally, we explored the bonding nature and magnetic alignment of EuS across these interfaces. Our findings indicate that the magnetic moments of EuS atoms are strongly influenced by the specific interface geometry and bonding arrangement.

This paper presents an efficient way to categorize all possible Borel Wadge classes. Building on the foundational work of Saint-Raymond and Saint-Raymond, our method is primarily driven by the concept of continuous open maps. Specifically, we demonstrate that every such Borel set can be expressed as the preimage of a basic open or closed set under a continuous function. Furthermore, our approach is highly effective in handling pairs of sets, as it allows us to determine the relative Wadge degrees of two sets by examining the function that maps one to the other's complement.

Recent advances in deep learning have yielded impressive performance, yet the substantial memory and computational requirements of these models often exceed the capabilities of practical deployment environments. While neural network pruning has emerged as a viable solution for accelerating inference, existing methods typically focus on achieving high compression ratios rather than delivering precise speedups aligned with specific hardware constraints. This paper introduces **ClickTrain**, an end-to-end fine-grained architecture-preserving pruning framework designed to accelerate the training of specific models on particular hardware. ClickTrain employs a novel pruning criterion based on the dynamic identification of "clicks"—operations that transition a computational graph from dense to sparse structures. By integrating this criterion into the backpropagation process, the approach enables effective training on pruned architectures. Empirical results demonstrate that ClickTrain delivers training speed improvements of up to 4.1× for ResNet-50 on an NVIDIA V100 GPU and 2.8× for BERT-Base on an Intel Xeon Gold 6248 CPU. Furthermore, the method achieves state-of-the-art latency, reaching convergence in just 0.6× the time required by prior methods, all without demanding modifications to standard training pipelines.

This paper investigates the modal extensions of the non-associative linear logic, focusing on modal functions within the order and topological semantics of complete lattices. We demonstrate that the distributive complete Lambek calculus, when equipped with modal operators, validates Kripke-style semantics. Furthermore, we establish key properties of this system, including the completeness theorem with respect to this semantics and the decidability of its axiomatic calculus.

Neutron star–black hole (NSBH) mergers represent a newly identified class of compact object mergers detected by gravitational wave observatories. These systems are characterized by a binary configuration where a neutron star merges with a black hole, driven by the Lense-Thirpre precession of the neutron star's orbit, which modulates the emitted gravitational wave signal. This study introduces a deep learning framework designed to identify and classify NSBH mergers within detector data. The method employs a convolutional neural network (CNN) to detect signals and a support vector machine (SVM) to classify them. The CNN utilizes a dataset comprising simulated signals from neutron star–black hole mergers, neutron star–white dwarf mergers, and non-astrophysical noise. The SVM is subsequently trained on this data to distinguish genuine merger signals from noise and other merger types. The results indicate that the combined deep learning approach successfully identifies NSBH mergers with 99.9% accuracy and classifies them correctly 99.4% of the time.

We report the discovery of an ancient hot Jupiter, TOI-5542 b, utilizing data from the TESS mission, ground-based photometry, and multi-band ground-based spectroscopy. TOI-5542 b exhibits a radius of $1.21 \pm 0.05 R_{\rm J}$, a mass of $0.82 \pm 0.10 M_{\rm J}$, an orbital period of $2.92$ days, and an equilibrium temperature of $1200$ K. The host star, a G-dwarf with a precise age of $10.1 \pm 0.3$ Gyr, displays a metal-deficient composition ($[\rm{Fe/H}] = -0.41 \pm 0.05$ dex) and a metal-poor atmosphere ($[\rm{M/H}] = -0.41 \pm 0.05$ dex). This system is notable for being the first to host a hot Jupiter orbiting a metal-poor, ancient star. Furthermore, the planet's mass-radius relationship aligns with predictions from the 2016 Fortney et al. model for a hydrogen/helium-dominated composition.

This study addresses a class of decision-making problems where a sequence of choices must be made under constraints, with each choice occurring in an environment drawn from a specific distribution. The objective is to minimize the selected criteria while adhering to the limits as closely as possible to the optimal strategy. The authors introduce a novel, efficient, and practical dual-based algorithm designed to generate near-optimal decision-making procedures. The method's performance is validated through simulations on two practical applications: a portfolio selection model with a fixed budget and a constrained selection task for a product. The results demonstrate that the proposed procedure yields performance very close to the theoretical optimum.

This paper outlines a methodology for recognizing offline handwritten mathematical notation through deep learning. We present the initial utilization of ResNet architectures for this specific domain, leveraging them to extract features from isolated mathematical symbols. These extracted features subsequently feed into a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network to model the sequence of symbols, thereby generating the complete mathematical expression. The proposed framework was evaluated using a newly established dataset, the HMNOR-MTEX, which contains 1,000 rendered expressions created from random combinations of 1,000 distinct characters. This corpus was split into training, validation, and testing sets with sizes of 800, 100, and 100 examples respectively. The system achieved an F1 score of 0.8100 on the test set, a result that surpasses previous approaches relying on traditional computer vision and statistical techniques.

We demonstrate that the expansion of the sheaf cohomology for a specific line bundle on a Fano complete intersection within projective space can be computed using an explicit supersymmetric quantum mechanics (SQM) framework. In this context, the expansion coefficients correspond to the partition function of a particular matrix model. We provide both generic formulas and explicit examples for the expansion of the sheaf cohomology associated with twisted $Q$-cycles.

Interactions among agents within social networks are pivotal in driving the spread of behaviors, opinions, and innovations. While it is established that the temporal duration of these interactions is non-trivial, their variability has received little attention. This study examines the fluctuations in interaction duration across diverse network structures, revealing that the second moment of the duration distribution is highly sensitive to the presence of a central hub. Furthermore, we demonstrate that hubs induce significant heterogeneity in interaction times connected to them, regardless of the specific network type or the distribution governing the base duration.

Recent advancements in reinforcement learning (RL) have introduced neural network-based methods that leverage sampling techniques like Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) to enhance exploration. However, these approaches often incur significant computational costs. This study introduces a novel actor-critic RL framework capable of learning optimal policies by employing the efficient Metropolis-Hastings algorithm within the sampling process. We further extend this work by integrating the Hamiltonian Monte Carlo method to refine the network's proposal distribution, thereby accelerating learning. Experimental evaluations across three benchmark environments demonstrate that our proposed method surpasses current state-of-the-art techniques in both performance and computational speed.
